My life isn‘t boring!“ #9: Thank you for your order. / Auto-Renewal starts now. / “Noooo!!“ Have you ever bought something online after seeing a message such as “Hurry! One item left!” even though you didn’t intend to buy it? Or have you ever felt rushed into making a purchase because of a limited-time offer? If you have, then you may have fallen prey to a dark pattern. Dark patterns are manipulative designs on websites and applications that trick users into making unintended decisions. These deceptive practices often have consequences that cause financial damages to the users. A widely used dark pattern is the practice of “forced continuity,” which requires users to pay a membership fee after a free trial ends. Companies deliberately avoid informing users about the end of the free trial period or make the cancellation process complicated. As a result, users have to pay membership fees even if they no longer want to use the service. Another common type of dark pattern is known as “hidden fees.” This design suddenly adds extra fees at the last step of the ordering process. On the final page, consumers are surprised to discover additional charges, such as shipping or processing fees, which the seller has added to increase the final cost of the order. “Confirm-shaming” is another online trick that users should be aware of. This technique manipulates users into feeling ashamed for cancelling their membership or requesting a refund for an order. Companies use this to keep their members subscribed, even if it goes against the members’ intentions. For example, when users want to cancel their subscription, they are offered two options: “I want to keep my benefits” and “I want to give up my benefits.” The first option is presented in an appealing way, while the second option seems like a bad choice. Dark Patterns: Deception or Marketing Strategy? / Companies and critics hold conflicting views on this issue. No! Not again! I hit the payment button! / Sss... thank you, Sssteve... One of my ssspecial, sssneaky dark patterns... sss... Dark patterns on digital platforms are becoming more complex and more prevalent. So, what is driving their growth? Over the years, online commerce has grown steadily, especially with the development of smart phones and other digital technologies. As the competition in online markets has intensified, companies have begun to develop sneakier strategies to trick people into making purchases. While these companies insist that they are simply using new types of marketing strategies, critics do not agree that dark patterns are valid marketing strategies. Rather, they suggest that a real marketing strategy create value for both companies and customers, promoting positive and supportive relationships. Dark patterns, in contrast, not only manipulate customers to act against their intentions, but they can also lead to financial losses and personal data leaks. To tackle this problem, extensive research across various websites and applications is being conducted to document the prevalence of dark patterns and come up with solutions. In addition to research, governments are actively discussing how to regulate these deceptive design patterns. The EU’s Digital Service Act, which banned dark patterns on online platforms in 2022, is a good example of such regulation in this area. Such regulations are expected to increase, limiting companies’ deceptive marketing practices in the digital market. However, regulations alone may not be sufficient. As individuals, we should take steps to combat dark patterns and be responsible for our online shopping behavior. This includes being cautious while making purchases, reading terms and conditions carefully, and recognizing that companies’ interests may not be the same as our own. Developing an awareness of dark patterns is also essential to avoid potential harm and economic loss. Ultimately, our attention and efforts will protect us from manipulation and enable us to make wise decisions in this digital age.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② are surprising → are surprised: 사람이 감정을 '느끼는' 쪽이면 과거분사(-ed)를 쓴다
det.analysis:
① suddenly adds: 주어 'This design(이 디자인)'은 단수라서 동사도 단수형 adds가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② consumers are surprising → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! '소비자들이 추가 요금을 발견하고 놀란다'라는 뜻이에요. 사람이 감정을 '느끼는' 쪽일 때는 과거분사(be surprised)를 써요. surprising(놀라게 하는)은 사물이 주어일 때 쓰는 형태라 사람 주어 consumers에는 surprised가 맞아요. ❌ surprising은 틀림 ←정답

③ technique manipulates: 주어 'This technique(이 기법)'가 단수라서 동사도 단수형 manipulates가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ goes against: 'even if it goes against ~'에서 주어 it이 단수라 동사도 단수형 goes가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 감정 표현: 사람이 느끼면 -ed(surprised), 사물이 감정을 일으키면 -ing(surprising)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ enabling → enable: 조동사 will 뒤에서 protect와 대등하게 연결되므로 동사원형을 쓴다
det.analysis:
① be responsible: 'we should take steps ~ and be responsible'에서 조동사 should 뒤에 take와 be가 and로 대등하게 연결돼요. 조동사 뒤라 둘 다 동사원형(take, be)이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② reading terms: 'being cautious ~, reading terms ~, and recognizing ~'는 동명사(-ing) 세 개가 나란히 연결된 병렬 구조예요. reading이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

③ Developing an awareness: 'Developing an awareness of dark patterns is ~'에서 동명사구가 문장의 주어예요. 동명사 주어는 단수 취급이라 뒤에 is가 온 것도 자연스러워요. ✅ 올바름

④ enabling us to make → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'our attention and efforts will protect us ~ and enable us to make ~'에서 조동사 will 뒤에 protect와 enable이 and로 대등하게 연결돼요. 앞이 동사원형 protect니까 뒤도 원형 enable이어야 하는데 enabling으로 써서 틀렸어요. ❌ enabling은 틀림 ←정답
det.tip: 조동사(will/should) 뒤 동사들이 and로 연결되면 전부 동사원형으로 맞춘다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① into make → into making: 전치사 into 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)를 쓴다
det.analysis:
① to trick people into make → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'to trick people into ~ purchases(사람들을 속여 구매하게 하다)'에서 into는 전치사예요. 전치사 뒤에는 동사원형이 아니라 동명사(-ing)를 써야 하므로 making이 맞는데 make로 써서 틀렸어요. ❌ make는 틀림 ←정답

③ promoting positive: 'creates value ~, promoting positive ~ relationships'는 앞 문장을 부연하는 분사구문(-ing)이에요. promoting이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

det.tip: 전치사(into/for/of) 뒤 동사는 항상 동명사(-ing)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ are expecting → are expected: 규제가 '늘어날 것으로 예상되는' 대상이므로 수동태를 쓴다
det.analysis:
① To tackle: 'To tackle this problem(이 문제를 해결하기 위해)'은 목적을 나타내는 to부정사예요. 문장 앞에서 '~하기 위해'로 쓰여 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② actively discussing: 'governments are actively discussing ~'는 현재진행형(be동사+-ing)이에요. 정부가 지금 논의하고 있다는 뜻이라 discussing이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

③ is a good example: 주어 'The EU's Digital Service Act(EU의 디지털 서비스법)'가 단수라 동사도 단수형 is가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ are expecting to increase → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'Such regulations are ~ to increase(그런 규제가 늘어날 것으로 예상된다)'에서 규제는 사람이 '예상하는' 대상이지 스스로 예상하는 게 아니에요. 그래서 수동태 are expected(예상되다)를 써야 하는데 능동형 are expecting으로 써서 틀렸어요. ❌ are expecting은 틀림 ←정답
det.tip: be expected to+동사원형: ~할 것으로 예상되다 (수동)

det.analysis:
① trick users(사용자를 속이다): 다크패턴은 사용자를 속여 원치 않는 결정을 하게 만든다는 문맥이라 trick이 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절

② consequences(결과·영향): '이런 기만적 관행은 사용자에게 금전적 피해를 주는 결과를 낳는다'라는 문맥이라 consequences가 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절

④ no longer want(더 이상 원하지 않는다): '더 이상 서비스를 이용하고 싶지 않아도 회원비를 내야 한다'라는 문맥이라 no longer want가 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절
det.tip: pay a fee = 요금을 내다 / receive = 받다 (돈의 방향이 반대)

det.korean: ① hide → document: 연구는 다크패턴 실태를 '기록·규명하려고' 수행되므로 document가 맞다
det.analysis:

② such regulation(그런 규제): EU의 디지털 서비스법을 '그런 규제의 좋은 예'라고 부르는 문맥이라 regulation이 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절

③ carefully(주의 깊게): '약관을 주의 깊게 읽어야 한다'라는 문맥이라 carefully가 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절

④ essential to avoid(피하기 위해 필수적인): '피해를 피하려면 다크패턴에 대한 인식을 기르는 것이 필수적이다'라는 문맥이라 essential이 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절
det.tip: document = (실태를) 기록·규명하다 ↔ hide = 숨기다 (문맥상 정반대)

det.tip: or로 연결된 빈칸은 앞 어구(avoid informing)와 같은 방향(사용자에게 불리)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

questions.passage: Dark patterns on digital platforms are becoming more complex and more prevalent.  So, what is driving their growth? Rather, they suggest that a real marketing strategy create value for both companies and customers, promoting positive and supportive relationships. det.analysis:

비평가들은 진정한 마케팅 전략이 기업과 고객 모두에게 가치를 창출한다고 본다.

questions.passage: “ Have ①<u>you ever bought</u> something online after seeing a message such as “Hurry!  One item left! ” even though you ②<u>didn’t intend buying</u> it?  Or have you ever ③<u>felt rushed into making</u> a purchase because of a limited-time offer?  If you have, then you ④<u>may have fallen</u> prey to a dark pattern.  Dark patterns are manipulative designs on websites and applications that trick users into making unintended decisions.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② intend buying → intend to buy: intend는 to부정사를 목적어로 취한다
det.analysis:
① you ever bought: 'Have you ever bought ~?'는 '~해 본 적 있나요?'라는 현재완료(경험) 의문문이에요. bought(과거분사)가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② didn't intend buying → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'you didn't intend ___ it(그것을 살 생각이 없었다)'에서 동사 intend(~하려고 하다)는 뒤에 'to+동사원형'을 목적어로 데려와요. 그래서 to buy가 맞는데 buying(동명사)으로 써서 틀렸어요. ❌ buying은 틀림 ←정답

③ felt rushed into making: 'felt rushed into making a purchase(서둘러 구매하도록 내몰린 느낌)'에서 into는 전치사라 뒤에 동명사 making이 와서 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ may have fallen: 'you may have fallen prey to ~(~의 먹잇감이 되었을지도 모른다)'는 'may have+과거분사(과거 일에 대한 추측)' 구문이에요. fallen이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: intend / want / hope + to부정사 (동명사 아님)

det.tip: 콤마 뒤에서 '~하면서'로 앞 내용을 부연하면 현재분사(-ing) 분사구문

questions.passage: A widely used dark pattern is the practice of “forced continuity,” which requires users to pay a membership fee after a free trial ends.  Companies deliberately avoid informing users about the end of the free trial period or make the cancellation process complicated.  As a result, users have to pay membership fees even if they no longer want to use the service.  Another common type of dark pattern is known as “hidden fees. ” This design suddenly adds extra fees at the last step of the ordering process.  On the final page, consumers are surprised to discover additional charges, such as shipping or processing fees, which the seller has added to increase the final cost of the order.  “Confirm-shaming” is another online trick that users should be aware of.  This technique manipulates users into feeling ashamed for cancelling their membership or requesting a refund for an order.  Companies use this to keep their members subscribed, even if it goes against the members’ intentions.  For example, when users want to cancel their subscription, they are offered two options: “I want to keep my benefits” and “I want to give up my benefits. ” The first option is presented in an appealing way, while the second option seems like a bad choice.

이 글은 '강제 연속(forced continuity)', '숨은 요금(hidden fees)', '확인 수치심(confirm-shaming)'이라는 대표적인 다크패턴 유형을 하나씩 들며 각각이 어떻게 사용자를 속이는지 설명해요.

✅ ④ common types of dark patterns and how they trick users: 세 가지 유형과 그 속임 방식을 그대로 담은 주제예요. ←정답
det.tip: 세 가지 예시(forced continuity/hidden fees/confirm-shaming) = 다크패턴 유형 소개

questions.passage: To tackle this problem, extensive research across various websites and applications is being conducted to document the prevalence of dark patterns and come up with solutions.  In addition to research, governments are actively discussing how to regulate these deceptive design patterns.  The EU’s Digital Service Act, which banned dark patterns on online platforms in 2022, is a good example of such regulation in this area.  Such regulations are expected to increase, limiting companies’ deceptive marketing practices in the digital market.  However, regulations alone may not be sufficient.  As individuals, we should take steps to combat dark patterns and be responsible for our online shopping behavior.  This includes being cautious while making purchases, reading terms and conditions carefully, and recognizing that companies’ interests may not be the same as our own.  Developing an awareness of dark patterns is also essential to avoid potential harm and economic loss.  Ultimately, our attention and efforts will protect us from manipulation and enable us to make wise decisions in this digital age.

✅ ② 규제(regulation)와 개인의 주의(being cautious)·책임(be responsible)을 함께 강조한 글의 결론과 일치해요. ←정답
